landmarks.name: Mount Yasur
landmarks.writeup: An active volcano on Tanna Island, known for its frequent eruptions and accessible lava lake.

wiki.extract: Mount Yasur is an active volcano on Tanna Island, Vanuatu, 361 m (1,184 ft) high above sea level, on the coast near Sulphur Bay, northeast of the taller Mount Tukosmera, which was active in the Pleistocene. It has a largely unvegetated pyroclastic cone with a nearly circular summit crater 400 m in diameter.

landmarks.name: Mele Cascades
landmarks.writeup: A series of beautiful waterfalls near Port Vila, popular for swimming and hiking.

wiki.extract: Efate, originally named Sandwich Island and also known as Île Vate or just Vate, is an island in the Pacific Ocean. It is part of the Shefa Province in Vanuatu, and the capital city, Port Vila, is located on the island.

landmarks.name: Chief Roi Mata's Domain
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site encompassing archaeological sites related to a powerful 16th-century chief.

wiki.extract: Roi Mata was a chiefly title in the central islands of Vanuatu. It was borne by a long dynasty of chiefs, from the 11th to the 17th century.

cultural_events.name: Naghol (Land Diving)
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional ritual on Pentecost Island where men jump from tall wooden towers with vines tied to their ankles.

cultural_events.name: Fest'Napuan
cultural_events.writeup: An annual music and cultural festival in Port Vila celebrating Vanuatu's diverse cultures and arts.

food_writeup: Vanuatu cuisine features root crops like taro and yam, fresh seafood, tropical fruits, and traditional dishes such as lap lap, a baked pudding made from grated root vegetables.
brief_history: Vanuatu was first settled by Melanesian people around 3,000 years ago. It was colonized by both Britain and France in the 19th century, becoming the New Hebrides Condominium. Vanuatu gained independence in 1980.

important_people.name: Walter Lini
important_people.description: First Prime Minister and independence leader

current_conflicts: Vanuatu is generally peaceful with no significant internal or external conflicts at present.
